Ferritins, ribonucleotide-reductase-like diiron proteins, and manganese catalases are separate families within the Ferritin-like superfamily, SCOPe a.25.1, which sits in the Ferritin-like fold a.25 of the all-alpha class. The superfamily grouping means their ferritin-like four-helix-bundle domains are judged to have a common evolutionary origin even though their active sites have diverged: ferritins are iron-storage/ferroxidase proteins, the ribonucleotide-reductase-like group includes diiron-carboxylate radical-generating oxygenases such as RNR R2-type proteins, and manganese catalases use a dimanganese center to disproportionate peroxide. The right transfer is therefore the conserved structural core and broad metal-binding architecture; it is unsafe to transfer ferritin iron-storage function, RNR radical chemistry, manganese-catalase substrate chemistry, oligomeric state, or metal specificity across these families without direct biochemical evidence. A representative or template from one family can support modeling of the ferritin-like helical bundle, but it should be treated as a remote template for the other named families rather than evidence that the target performs the same reaction.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
